issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency: the interface for milking is referred to as 'Milkable' in the problem statement and template (expects method messageOnMilk()), but the solution repository defines an interface named 'Dairy' (declaring messageOnMilk()) and leaves Milkable.java empty. Seal and Goat in the solution implement 'Dairy' rather than 'Milkable'. This mismatch means code or tests that expect a 'Milkable' type (as described in the spec and used in the template Main) will not interoperate with the solution classes and can cause compilation/type errors or confusion for students about which interface to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the milking interface name consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: rename the solution's Dairy interface to Milkable (update the file name to Milkable.java and the interface declaration to 'public interface Milkable { String messageOnMilk(); }'), and change Seal and Goat to implement Milkable. Remove or repurpose the empty Milkable.java in the solution. Alternatively, if you prefer 'Dairy', update the problem statement and template to refer to Dairy everywhere. Ensure the interface declares messageOnMilk() with the exact signature specified in the problem statement so template, spec, and solution align.

issues.description: The exercise describes and the template use an interface named 'Milkable' with method messageOnMilk(), but the solution repository defines the same concept with a differently named interface 'Dairy' (public interface Dairy { String messageOnMilk(); }) and the concrete classes Goat and Seal implement 'Dairy'. Additionally the solution repo contains an (essentially) empty Milkable.java file. This identifier mismatch (Milkable vs Dairy) represents the same conceptual behavior (milkable animals) but uses different names across artifacts, making it unclear which identifier students should implement or reference and increasing cognitive load when mapping the problem requirements to the solution/template code.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name across all artifacts so the conceptual entity has a single identifier. Preferred fix: rename the solution's 'Dairy' interface to 'Milkable' (file Dairy.java -> Milkable.java) and update Goat and Seal to implement Milkable. Remove the empty Milkable.java file from the solution (or replace it with the renamed interface) and ensure the method signature remains 'String messageOnMilk()'. Alternatively, if the project prefers 'Dairy', update the problem statement and template references from 'Milkable' to 'Dairy' so all artifacts use the same name.
